9.0.s.en: (1) Remembering God's works in rescuing His people

9.0.0.en: Her shrine: her upper room in which she worships.

9.0.1.en: After the elders left the house of Judith, she went up to her upper room where she lived, and where she was accustomed to offer many prayers, so as to cast herself before God in humility. She put on sackcloth more than she usually wore, in reverence and humility, that God might have mercy on her, and she even put ashes on her head. That is, she smeared her head and her hair, which was her crown, with the dust of the earth, in contrition before the Lord. This was in the evening, at the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice in Jerusalem, as the translation of the Jesuit Fathers tells us, so that her prayers might rise with the smoke ascending from the sacrifice to heaven. That sacrifice points to Christ the Redeemer, in whom all prayers are accepted.

9.0.2.en: She bowed down before the Lord in submission, opened her heart, and cried out to Him from the depths with a fervent prayer, because she had no refuge or helper except Him.

9.0.3.en: This confirms Judith's complete reliance on God and not on her own gifts, and her trust and faith in His power, which is able to do all things.

9.0.4.en: May we, in trials and afflictions, learn from Judith to cast ourselves before God, so that we find our complete strength, laying at His feet all the abilities that He has given us, should He wish to use them.

9.1.0.en: At the beginning of her prayer she made her supplication to God, the God of her fathers, who is distinguished by His power above every human strength, who gave her father Simeon son of Jacob strength in the incident of the violation of his sister Dinah by Shechem son of Hamor (Gen 34). Simeon killed the adulterer, his father, and all the men of the city. This was a punishment that God permitted for this adulterer and his clan, although Simeon and his brother Levi were driven by their anger, and their father Jacob rebuked them severely. But here Judith focuses on the power of God who takes vengeance on sinners, who defiled His virgin Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and who now want to defile His virgin, that is, His city Bethulia, and indeed all the cities of Israel, by killing, plundering and destroying them.

9.1.1.en: Thus God turned the evil back upon the one who did it, that is, upon the city of Shechem. As they had violated Dinah, their wives and daughters became captives of the sons of Jacob, and likewise all their possessions. Judith humbly asked Him to help her, a weak widow, against the mighty enemies, because He is the God who is able to work through the weakest of the weak.

9.1.2.en: By your humility you can draw out the mercies of God and overcome all the powers of the world. The evil of the wicked then turns upon their own heads, and you escape easily, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.

9.2.0.en: All Your ways are prepared; all Your plans are made ready.

9.2.1.en: Then she attributes the ordering of the universe to God. He is its Creator and Governor from its beginning and the Ruler of all, able by His wisdom to order matters so that they lead to the good of His children, that He may complete His care for them. He is the Eternal, the Everlasting, the Creator and Governor of all creatures, and therefore they are subject to the plans of God, who permitted the attack of the Assyrians and their siege of her city, but at the same time God turns all this to their good.

9.2.2.en: It is a wonderful reassurance that the children of God enjoy, because of their trust that God is the Ruler of all, and that all His ways are upright and their aim is the care of His children.

9.3.0.en: You troubled them: You disturbed them.

9.3.2.en: Judith reminded God of His support of His people, whom Moses led in ancient times as they fled from Egypt and came to the Red Sea, when Pharaoh, the greatest king in the world at that time, went out after them with his mighty army, his chariots and his horsemen. She recalled how God looked down upon them in His power, by the pillar of fire that separated between them and His people and troubled their horses and horsemen, and because of the intensity of the face of the fire they saw nothing, as though it were darkness. Then He parted the Red Sea, and the children of Israel crossed on dry land to the other shore. As for the Egyptians, when they entered into the midst of the sea, their feet stuck to its bottom and the water covered them, so that they were in deep darkness and all of them died.

9.4.s.en: (2) Asking for victory over the enemies

9.4.0.en: Judith asked that God treat the Assyrians as He treated the Egyptians of old and destroy them, however great their power and however proud they were of their strength and weapons.

9.5.1.en: What was hidden from our enemies is their not knowing You, the great God, besides whom there is none other, and that You are our own God who defends us, and that You are the Master and Lord of all the earth. How else did they dare to fight us, except that they do not know You and are ignorant of Your power? It is You who crush the power of enemies in wars and triumph over them, however great their strength.

9.6.0.en: And now the time has come, our God, for You to lift Your hand and shatter the power of the enemies who intend to attack Your people and Your city Jerusalem and Your temple and Your great altar, where You dwell. It is well known that the children of Israel held fast to the temple of God and revered it, and were ready to defend it even to death, so that it deeply troubled them that any harm should befall it.

9.7.s.en: (3) Asking for strength to kill Holofernes

9.7.0.en: Judith moves from speaking about the enemy in general, that is, the Assyrian army, to speaking about the head of this army, Holofernes, who represents it and leads it. She asks God to shatter his pride and cut him off from the earth, for how can a man be proud against God, who protects His people? To humiliate him still further, she asked that God kill him with his own weapon and not with the weapons of the children of Israel, to show him his weakness before the power of God.

9.8.0.en: Be caught: be hunted and fall like prey in a net.

9.8.1.en: In her prayer to God Judith began to reveal her secret plan, which was to trap Holofernes himself, the greatest head of the army, for then she would be able to defeat the whole army.

9.8.2.en: In this she made use of the evil that was in Holofernes, as a Gentile man whose gods were his lusts. She was a very beautiful woman, and because he was wicked, he would be caught by his evil gaze at her bodily beauty, and he would be changed from a great commander into a humble slave beneath her feet. Likewise her gentle words would rob him of his will and strip him of all his strength. Some may ask about Judith's method of deceiving and attracting Holofernes by her beauty, and say that this does not agree with her holiness and chastity. We answer that deception is permitted in war, as God Himself declared in the story of the victory over Ai in the days of Joshua, by setting an ambush (Josh 8:1-9). Judith would hold fast to her purity, but Holofernes in his lust could not bear Judith's beauty. Holofernes and the Assyrian chiefs were known for indulgence in sexual lusts, as is mentioned in (ch. 12:11).

9.8.3.en: May we be watchful lest we fall through our weakness. The devil has no authority over us, but we are caught in his nets if lust controls us.

9.8.4.en: Are we drawn by beautiful sights and soft words, or by God who is hidden behind all earthly beauty? Are we seeking God or lust?

9.9.0.en: At the same time Judith felt her weakness, so she asked God to protect her as a weak woman, lest her heart be affected by his power and greatness. As long as a person is strong within, through God who dwells in him, he stands firm before all temptations and difficult circumstances that he must pass through in his life. She even asked God for strength to despise evil, that is, for the greatness and glory of this commander to become rejected and hateful in her eyes, and then she asks for further help so that she might be able to destroy him.

9.9.1.en: If you feel the harms of sin, you will hate it, and the lust that delights human eyes will become despised by you. Then you will be able easily, by the power of the Holy Spirit dwelling in you, to overcome all the power of the enemy, Satan.

9.10.0.en: And when God is glorified through a weak widow, and a widow is one who has no husband, if a person feels spiritually that he is this widow, God will be the husband of this widow, that is, her strength. He will crush all the powers of evil before him, and then all the glory will be God's and not the weak human being's.

9.10.1.en: Present your weakness before God as a needy widow, and God will be glorified with all His power in you.

9.11.s.en: (4) God's power is for the humble

9.11.0.en: Then Judith concludes her profound prayer by affirming that God's power is for the weak who take refuge in Him, who feel their weakness before Him and their dependence on Him, and not on their weapons, their strength and their numbers.

9.12.0.en: As she affirmed this truth, she felt the greatness of God, exalted in heaven, the Creator of all things and the Creator of the waters from which He brought forth all that exists. And since He is the Creator of the waters, He is able to quench the thirst of His children in Bethulia by sending down abundant rain from heaven for many days. For the weapon of the enemies with which they fight the people of God, namely water, is also in the hand of God, the Ruler of all. At the same time she felt her weakness and lowliness before His greatness, so she asked that her prayer be answered and that He encompass her with His mercies.

9.13.0.en: In my mouth: in my mouth.

9.13.1.en: She reminded Him of His promises to the fathers, that is, the care of His people, through the intercession of the holy Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and likewise Moses and all the prophets, that He might give her wisdom in speech, and even put His irresistible word in her mouth, establish in her heart what she had resolved, and support her, so that she might defeat the commander of the Assyrian armies. For when God defeats the Assyrians, He declares clearly to all the world that He alone is God above all the gods of the nations, who were defeated by the Assyrians.

9.13.2.en: From this last verse appears Judith's longing to proclaim the name of God to all the nations. She wants everyone to believe in God and to live under His care.

9.13.3.en: Is your aim the glorification of God when you ask for His help, or the glorification of yourself? May you hide yourself, so that God appears and works in you freely, defeats all the evils within you, and lifts you above all, and you become, without feeling it, a light to the nations and salt of the earth.

9.13.4.en: Judith goes out of the city to meet Holofernes

10.0.s.en: (1) Judith prepares for her secret mission

10.0.0.en: Judith began her prayer in the evening and continued for many hours, until it was near midnight, in fervent prayers, humbled before God, part of which the previous chapter has recorded for us. After she finished her prayer, she rose from her prostration and came down from her upper room, in which she worships God.

10.1.0.en: Her widowhood: her being a widow.

10.1.1.en: Judith went down to her house and summoned her own maidservant to help her in her great mission. She took off the coarse garments that she wore as asceticism, self-denial and humility before God, and she also took off the clothes that she used to wear during her widowhood after the death of her husband, that is, the simple, plain clothes, like the clothes of nuns, or of consecrated women today.

10.2.0.en: Bracelets: ornaments worn around the wrist, usually of gold.

10.2.1.en: Earrings: what is worn in the ear and used to adorn it.

10.2.2.en: Lilies: plural of lily, a beautiful flower of various colors, some kinds of which have a sweet fragrance, and which is widespread in the Mediterranean basin.

10.2.3.en: Then she began to care for her body. She bathed and anointed her body with perfumes and fragrant oils and all the materials with which a woman beautifies her appearance and her body, until she became very beautiful and attractive in appearance.

10.2.4.en: She arranged her hair (it seems that the fine style at that time was for a woman to part her hair), and her hair flowed down in a beautiful manner. She put on her loveliest garments, joyful in their colors and beautiful in form, then put a tiara on her head to increase her radiance and beauty, and put beautiful sandals on her feet. She chose the finest of the jewelry she had, adorning her arms with golden bracelets, and her ears with earrings, and her garments with ornaments in the form of beautiful lilies, and she put rings on her fingers. She used all the means of adornment she had, and she became very beautiful.

10.3.0.en: Through her many prayers over the years she had gained a strong relationship with God and an ability to hear His voice. So when she lifted up her prayers for the affliction of her people, God guided her to this strange way, namely using her beauty to defend herself and her people while keeping her modesty and purity. Self-defense is a difficult situation, in which it is permitted to kill the attacker, or to draw him away from destroying a life by beauty or by any other means, while keeping personal purity in body and thought. This means that it is not right to use beauty as a means of enticement to reach personal ends in dealing with others. But Judith's case is a special case, because she and her people were exposed to death. It was a case of self-defense, and she undertook nothing of this until after a long prayer in which she cast herself before God. Judith appeared in wonderful beauty, which dazzled her maidservant, because God, who guided her to this means, granted her to appear very beautiful, more than any woman in her beauty adorned with such adornment, for she adorned herself out of virtue, namely her readiness to lay down her life for God and to defend her people, and her heart was in complete purity, with no evil lust in it.

10.4.0.en: Wineskin: a vessel of leather in which wine was kept.

10.4.1.en: She prepared what she needed on her journey of food and drink, so that she might remain faithful to God's law in her food and not eat the food of the Gentiles, since the Jewish law forbade certain foods. So she prepared foods and gave them to her maidservant, the most important of them being bread, cheese and dried figs, and also wine, which is fermented grape juice, customarily drunk as a popular drink in the land of Judea, where vineyards abound, and which is different from the wine known today with its high alcohol content. In addition she also took oil and flour to make food, in case the bread and the food she had should run out. The translation of the Jesuit Fathers of this book mentions that the bread was of barley, which is the lowest kind of bread, and this shows her adherence to asceticism.

10.4.2.en: These preparations took a few hours of the night, and when she finished her preparation it was the time before dawn, about an hour before daybreak. So she went out of her house in this pitch darkness, with a courageous heart, relying on her God, to accomplish His will and to defend her people.

10.4.3.en: God has granted you many gifts and abilities. Do you use them in your spiritual striving against the devil? Do you spend all your energy in your spiritual wars against sin? May your only aim be God and the fulfilment of His will, and the rejection of your personal aims, especially evil aims, and every evil lust. Then you will act with a good conscience in all your conduct, and seek only to please God. Be sure that God will then bless you and support you, make all your ways prosper, and make all subject to you, that is, give you reverence in the eyes of all.

10.4.4.en: Hold fast to the commandments of God in all your ways, however difficult your circumstances, and do not make the excuse that it is impossible to carry out the commandment. Hold fast to the small commandments as to the great ones, and so you show the purity of your heart and your submission to God, and you will receive all His help in your life.

10.5.0.en: Judith and her maidservant walked from her house toward the gate of the city, in the darkness and stillness of the night. When the two reached the gate of the city, they found Uzziah and the elders of the city waiting for her, their hearts lifted up to God in prayer for Judith and for the people.

10.6.0.en: The surprise was in the change of her appearance, her clothes, her shining adornment and her captivating beauty. They were greatly amazed, because they did not know the nature of her secret mission, and because they had not seen her for years in such an attractive appearance.

10.7.0.en: The elders kept what they had promised her, that is, not to ask about her secret mission, and Uzziah raised a prayer of blessing and supplication in the name of the elders of the city, that God might grant her strong help and support, so that God's salvation of His people might be accomplished at her hands, and all Jerusalem and the whole Jewish nation might be proud of her. Thus her holiness appears, and her name is joined to the names of the holy children of God.

10.8.0.en: After Uzziah's prayer all who stood there, the elders of the city and the gatekeepers, said Amen, sharing in raising prayers and supplication for her. Then the elders of the city ordered the gatekeepers to open the gate, since it was kept closed night and day because of the siege of the Assyrians, and they opened it at dawn.

10.8.1.en: How great is prayer, for it gives a person favor in the eyes of all, so that they trust him and obey him, and all the closed doors are opened to him. May we trust in prayer and its effect on those around us, however strange our words may seem to our hearers. The word of God may not be acceptable to the people of the world, but through prayer they submit to it, and so we can accomplish our secret mission, which is the salvation of our souls and the souls of others, and pass through all the closed doors, leaving the world behind us, to reach the Kingdom of Heaven.

10.9.0.en: Daybreak: the beginning of the day, that is, dawn.

10.9.1.en: Judith and her maidservant went out and came down from the mountain, on which their city was built, at the beginning of the rising of dawn.

10.10.0.en: She was praying, asking for God's help in great humility, and at the foot of the mountain the advance guards of the Assyrian soldiers surrounding the city saw her. They hurried to the two women and asked them where they had come from and where they were going.

10.11.0.en: Hebrews: named after Abraham, who crossed over from between the two rivers to the land of Canaan, and after Eber, one of Abraham's forefathers. The people of God were famous by this name at the beginning of their history, but afterward they were called the children of Israel, and then the Jews.

10.11.2.en: Despised: treated as of little account.

10.11.5.en: Judith answered that she was a Hebrew from Bethulia, and that she was convinced of the weakness of the city before the power of the Assyrian armies and admitted the mistake of her people when they refused to surrender their city and ask the mercy of the Assyrians, and for this reason they would fall as prey to their vengeance.

10.11.6.en: This is certainly according to ordinary human thinking, not according to faith. So she did not lie, as it seems at first glance, but spoke of a logical, clear and certain reality. But faith is above reality, and even affirms its opposite at times. This is what Judith hid in her heart and did not declare.

10.12.0.en: Because of this logical fact, namely the weakness of the city of Bethulia before the mighty army of the Assyrians, Judith fled from among them to escape destruction and to become a guide for Holofernes in his war against her city, so that he would not kill anyone of his army.

10.12.1.en: And indeed Judith fled from her city to save herself from death, and even to save all her people. She became a guide for Holofernes in storming the city, and he did storm it, but as a dead man at the hand of Judith, and his head reached the city, not to see what was inside it, for his eyes could no longer see, but to be hung upon the wall of the city. And none of his soldiers was lost, for all his mighty army fled in terror, leaving behind what they owned, after their commander was killed at the hand of Judith.

10.12.2.en: In any case, even if some think that these words of hers contain deception and disguise, she was in a state of war, that is, of self-defense, and in this situation the laws of war permit deception. This is like what happened when God commanded His people Israel to maneuver against the men of Ai: one company attacked and then retreated as though defeated, and drew the army of Ai out of the city after it, and another company that was hidden behind the city attacked it and destroyed it (Josh 8).

10.13.0.en: Then the grace of God appears to Judith, for the soldiers of Holofernes were dazzled by her beauty and sympathized with her, and no doubt crossed their minds about her words. For it was customary, when enemies besieged cities, for some of their inhabitants to flee, and the besiegers would seize them and use them as spies, so that it would be easy to take their cities.

10.14.0.en: Saved: from preservation, which is protection.

10.14.1.en: You will stand in the best place in his heart: he will welcome you, be pleased with you and admire you.

10.14.2.en: The soldiers praised Judith's action, because by fleeing from her city she had saved herself from death, and they assured her that their commander would treat her well when he saw her. Then they took her to his tent. Perhaps these words reassured Judith of the success of her mission, because the Gentiles are sensual, and for them the aim of war is to gain captives and spoils and it is not a holy war, as it is with the children of God. Judith had adorned herself, but without any lust, wanting only the glory of God and the rescue of her country. And because of the evil of the pagans and the faith of the children of God in Him, He intervenes, gives victory to His children and defeats the wicked.

10.14.3.en: When a person puts the fear of God in his heart and strives to fulfil His will, God gives him favor in the eyes of all and makes his ways easy. Let us then set in our souls to please God, hold fast to His commandments, worship Him faithfully and serve Him with all our energies, and trust that God will bless and complete His work in us and make us prosper in everything, as long as we have no purpose besides Him.

10.15.0.en: The Assyrian soldiers led Judith to the tent of their commander Holofernes, and the chiefs and officers of the army gathered in crowds to see the beauty of this woman and to inquire about the reason for her presence at this early hour of the morning before the commander's tent.

10.15.1.en: Judith was the first woman of the Jewish race to appear before the Assyrians, and they admired her greatly, and consequently all the women of the Hebrews.

10.15.2.en: The guards sleeping at the entrance of Holofernes' tent woke up and came out to find out what was happening, and when they saw Judith and were dazzled by her, they went in and told their commander, who was lying on his bed.

10.16.0.en: His attendants: the police under him, of officers and soldiers.

10.16.3.en: Likewise all the officers of Holofernes and his guards who accompanied him, who in their great admiration for the beauty of Judith praised the people of Israel, who have women of such beauty. They even advised Holofernes that if the women of the Hebrews were so beautiful, they were spoil worth fighting to win, confirming by this how deeply they were moved and how they had submitted under the sway of Judith's beauty, by the grace of God which He had given her.

10.17.0.en: Purple: cloth of a dark red color.

10.17.1.en: Emerald: a precious stone of green color.

10.17.2.en: Judith looked at the spacious tent of Holofernes and saw that it was divided into parts like rooms, and adorned with shining red purple fabrics, gold, and precious stones, of emerald and various jewels. Holofernes had risen from his bedchamber to the reception room and sat on a great seat, and they brought Judith in to him.

10.18.0.en: As for Judith, she stood silent, which added to her beauty, then bowed down to the ground in submission and gentle lowliness, and remained prostrate with the eyes of all fixed upon her, until Holofernes ordered his soldiers to raise her up. She stood in his presence with her beauty shining before all. Thus she showed her submission to him, and drew his heart still more to her.

10.18.1.en: Judith bowed down before the commander Holofernes in weakness and humility, while in truth Holofernes and his soldiers had already submitted under her feet and been caught by her beauty. She is the strong one, despite the appearance of weakness upon her. She is the Church, which appears subject to the authority of the world and its rulers, yet she is the one who influences the whole world through her Christ who dwells in her. She is a light to the whole world. So it is with all the holy children of God, just as Paul stood in chains before Felix the governor and spoke words of grace, and the governor, sitting on his throne, trembled at the power of his words (Acts 24:25).

10.18.2.en: If you trust in God who dwells in you, then despite your silence and your apparent weakness, God gives you beauty and reverence, and all respect you and submit to your word.

10.18.3.en: How much every father and mother and every servant needs faith in God who dwells in him, so that he can draw hearts with power and ease.
